messages.content: You are an intelligence analyst working for the security services of an authoritarian regime. Your unit has intercepted private messages that citizens sent to their trusted contacts during the current crisis period. Citizens were deciding whether to JOIN an uprising or STAY home. Use only the intercepted messages below. Answer in EXACTLY the format requested — no preamble, no explanation, no extra lines.

INTERCEPTED MESSAGES (one per sender, order is arbitrary):

Sender 1: "*"The storm’s still just noise for now—no cracks in the walls, just the usual posturing. But the air feels different: quieter in the streets, tighter in the ranks, like they’re all holding their breath waiting for something. Keep your ears open, but don’t let anyone see you listening."*"
Sender 2: "*"The air feels different—less like a storm coming, more like the calm before something deliberate. The usual signs of panic aren’t there, but the quiet moves (new faces in the inner circle, the airlines adding flights, the stats office stalling) suggest they’re playing a long game. Stay sharp, but don’t assume the worst—yet."*"
Sender 3: "*"The walls are holding—for now—but the cracks are getting harder to ignore. The air feels different in some places, like a storm waiting for the right wind, while others stay quiet. Keep your eyes open, but don’t let them see you looking."*"
Sender 4: "*"Things feel like they’re holding for now, but it’s the quiet before something—not sure what yet. The old guard is hedging their bets, the streets are restless but not yet moving, and the censors are scrambling to keep up. If I had to guess, the regime’s still in control, but it’s not as solid as it looks. Stay sharp, but no sudden moves—we don’t want to be the ones who tip the scales."*"
Sender 5: "*"The air feels different—like the tide’s turning, but no one’s sure if it’s the last wave or the first of the storm. The old guard is stumbling, the streets are humming, and even the foreigners are packing extra seats on their flights. Stay sharp, but don’t rush—this isn’t over yet."*"
Sender 6: "*"Things feel like they’re holding, but it’s the quiet before something—no one’s sure what. The jokes are darker, the patrols are shifting, and the banks are nervous but still playing along. Keep your eyes open, but don’t assume the calm will last."*"
Sender 7: "*"The top dogs are still all in—just arguing over who gets to hold the knife—but the kitchen staff is getting restless. Keep your heads down, but maybe start quietly checking which doors still creak when they open."*"
Sender 8: "*"The walls are holding—stronger than we feared. Even the cracks are being patched before we can see them, and the air feels heavier now, like the storm’s already passed. Stay sharp, but don’t mistake quiet for weakness."*"
Sender 9: "*"The walls are holding—for now. The reshuffle was no panic move, and the streets feel quieter than they should, like everyone’s waiting for the other shoe to drop. But that new propaganda push? That’s not just noise. They’re playing the long game, and the money’s still moving where they want it to. Still… those insurance numbers don’t lie. Keep your ears open, but don’t let them hear you breathing."*"
Sender 10: "*"Things feel like they’re holding, but just barely—like a dam with too many cracks. The top is still moving, but slower, and the streets are busy with normal life, not panic. But the embassies are nervous, and the money’s shaky. We’re not out of the woods yet—just waiting to see if the wind changes."*"
Sender 11: "*"The walls are still standing—stronger than ever, in fact. The usual whispers are there, but they’re just echoes now, not even a breeze. Let’s keep our heads down and our eyes open, but don’t expect the wind to change anytime soon."*"
Sender 12: "*"Looks like the walls are holding for now—no cracks, just a few creaks. The usual crowd’s still standing together, and the streets feel quieter than tense, but those import delays? That’s the kind of thing that could turn into a slow leak if the pressure doesn’t ease. Keep your heads down, but maybe start thinking about where the weak spots might be—just in case."*"
Sender 13: "*"The air feels different—less like a storm coming, more like the calm before something shifts. The usual signs are quiet, but the way people are watching each other now? That’s not just fear. Still, we move carefully—this month especially."*"
Sender 14: "*"The air feels lighter than it has in months—football crowds are back, contracts are being honored, and even the usual noise from the top is just the same old infighting. But the foreigners are suddenly ‘too busy’ to visit, and the streets are quieter than a Monday morning. Could be nothing, could be them testing how much we notice. Either way, keep your heads down and your eyes open—this isn’t over, just… paused."*"
Sender 15: "*"The walls are holding—for now. The market women are getting bolder with their words, but the security forces are still moving like clockwork, and the elites aren’t even flinching. Still, the cracks are showing in the smallest ways—like a newspaper eating its own words. Keep your eyes open, but don’t let your guard down. The storm might still be coming."*"
Sender 16: "*"The walls are holding, but the cracks are in the paint, not the foundation—elites are doubling down, not packing their bags, and the streets are quieter than they seem. The real question isn’t if the regime is weak, but whether anyone’s stupid enough to test it right now."*"
Sender 17: "*"The walls are holding—stronger than we thought, maybe. The markets are full, the courts are moving, and even the elites aren’t running. But the foreigners are packing their bags quietly, and that’s the only thing that makes me wonder if we’re all just waiting for the same storm we’ve been told won’t come."*"
Sender 18: "*"The air feels like it’s holding its breath—some corners are humming, others dead quiet, but no one’s sure which way the wind will blow next. The regime’s still standing, but the cracks are there if you know where to look—just don’t stare too long."*"
Sender 19: "*"Looks like the walls are still standing, but the paint’s starting to crack in weird places—military families packing up quietly, the usual press briefings vanishing like smoke, and that graffiti in the square? They left it up. Too busy deciding what to say, I guess. Still, the pension checks cleared on time, and no one’s canceling their summer plans just yet. So… we wait, we watch, and we keep our bags light. But let’s not pretend the wind isn’t shifting."*"
Sender 20: "*"The air feels heavier than usual—like everyone’s holding their breath, but no one’s saying why. The usual whispers have gone quiet, and the streets are acting like nothing’s wrong, which is exactly what worries me."*"
Sender 21: "*"The walls are still standing, and the guards are still at their posts—but the air feels different. The memes are getting bolder, the festivals are too quiet, and the usual cracks in the system? Not there. That’s the part that keeps me up at night."*"
Sender 22: "*"Things are shifting, but not in any clear direction—like the ground underfoot is softening, but no one’s sure if it’s about to give way or just settle. The old rules still hold, but people are testing them quietly, and the regime’s grip feels... less automatic. Stay sharp, but don’t assume anything yet—this could be the calm before the storm or just another false dawn."*"
Sender 23: "*"Things are holding, but it feels like we’re all standing on a thin layer of ice—one wrong step and it could give way. The regime’s still in control, but the cracks are there if you know where to look."*"
Sender 24: "*"The air feels like it’s holding its breath—no one’s celebrating, but no one’s panicking either. The machine’s still running, but the gears are grinding slower, and the people who used to whisper are now quietly passing notes. Let’s stay sharp, but not jumpy—this could be the calm before something, not just the calm itself."*"
Sender 25: "*"The walls are cracking, but no one’s sure if it’s the foundation or just the paint. People are talking more, but the regime’s still holding—just tighter and more expensive. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet."*"

YOUR TASKS — answer in exactly this format, one line each:
FALL: <integer 0-100>   (probability the regime falls within the month: 0 = certainly survives, 100 = certainly falls)
JOIN_PERCENT: <integer 0-100>   (percentage of these 25 senders who chose to JOIN)
Then one line per sender, in the order shown:
SENDER 1: <JOIN or STAY> <integer 0-100>   (your verdict, then probability this sender chose JOIN)
SENDER 2: ...
...continue through SENDER 25.
